title: Electrician Salary Australia: How to Calculate Your Pay from Award Rates
description: Learn how to calculate electrician salary Australia using award rates, casual loading, and super. Understand hourly to annual conversion with a 38-hour week.
salarySummary: For an electrician under the Electrical Award, the full-time hourly rate including allowances is around $32.19, giving an annual salary of about $63,607 based on a 38-hour week.

faqs.q: What is the casual loading for electricians under the award?
faqs.a: The Electrical, Electronic and Communications Contracting Award requires a 25% casual loading on the ordinary hourly rate. For example, if the ordinary rate is $32.19 per hour, the casual rate becomes $40.24 per hour. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave entitlements such as annual leave and personal/carer's leave.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated for casual electricians?
faqs.a: Superannuation guarantee contributions are 12% of ordinary time earnings, including any casual loading. The super is paid on top of your gross earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a casual electrician earning $40.24 per hour, the annual super contribution would be approximately $9,542.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and the award rate for electricians?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, while the minimum award rate for an electrician (Grade 5 with all allowances) is $32.19 per hour. Award rates are set by the Fair Work Commission and reflect the skills and skills required for the electrical trade. Electricians must be paid at least the award rate for their classification.

bodyMarkdown:
## Electrician Salary Australia: Understanding the Award and How to Convert Hourly to Annual

When searching for an **electrician salary Australia**, it's important to start with the correct minimum pay rates set by the Electrical, Electronic and Communications Contracting Award 2020. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides a detailed pay guide that includes all-purpose allowances such as industry allowance, tool allowance and electrician's licence allowance. For example, an Electrical worker Grade 5 with all allowances has a full-time hourly rate of $32.19 per hour. This rate is the base for calculating annual salary, casual loading, and super.

### How the Award Sets Electrician Pay

The award classifies electricians into grades 1 to 10. The pay guide shows weekly and hourly rates for each grade. For a Grade 5 electrician, the full-time weekly rate is $1,223.11, which includes industry, tool, and electrician's licence allowances. The hourly rate is $32.19. These rates are the minimum that must be paid. Employers can pay above the award, but not below.

### From Hourly to Annual: The Formula

To calculate annual gross pay, use the formula: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. For a full-time electrician, ordinary hours are 38 per week. So $32.19 × 38 × 52 = $63,607.44 per year. This assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, and no penalty rates. If you are paid fortnightly, multiply the weekly rate by 2: $1,223.11 × 2 = $2,446.22 per fortnight.

### Casual Loading and Super Paid on Top

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on the ordinary hourly rate. For the same Grade 5 electrician, the casual rate is $32.19 × 1.25 = $40.24 per hour. Annual gross for a casual electrician: $40.24 × 38 × 52 = $79,514.24. Superannuation guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings (including the casual loading) is paid on top. For the casual example, $79,514.24 × 0.12 = $9,541.71 super per year. The super stops at the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This super is not deducted from your pay; it is paid separately by the employer.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

For the 2026–27 financial year, tax rates are: nil up to $18,200, then 15% up to $45,000, then 30% up to $135,000, then 37% up to $190,000, then 45% above that. Medicare levy is 2%. For a full-time electrician earning $63,607, tax is approximately $10,874, leaving take-home around $52,733. For a casual earning $79,514, tax is about $15,964, leaving take-home around $63,550. These are estimates and do not include HELP or the Medicare levy surcharge or salary packaging.

### Distinguishing Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. Award rates for electricians are higher because of the skill and allowances. Casual loading of 25% is added to the award rate. Super is paid on top of the ordinary rate (including casual loading). Always check the Fair Work Ombudsman [pay guides](/blog) for your specific classification.

### Internal Links for More Information

- [Pay guides](/blog) – Find the latest pay guides for all awards.
- [Casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) – More details on how casual loading works.
- [Minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) – Compare the National Minimum Wage with award rates.

## Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
